packageRules.description: Don't update vendored upstream CI under external/*/.circleci/. We don't run it; subrepo pulls overwrite any edits.
Group non-major npm updates; weekly lockfile maintenance runs out-of-band

Major updates: one PR per package (API breaks reviewed individually). groupName: null overrides any inherited monorepo group from config:recommended's group:monorepos / group:recommended presets. Applies to customManagers (WiX) as well — by design; the customManagers block has no groupName, so this just reasserts the default.
gsudo (installer-E2E de-elevation): auto-merge; the required Test installer check gates it.

Tauri ships each plugin as an npm/crate pair and `npx tauri build` refuses a major.minor mismatch (#679). The npm and cargo managers are grouped separately above, so without this a bump on one side lands alone and breaks the DMG bundle. Last rule wins, so this overrides those groups for these packages.

Vendored git-subrepo deps (v2ray-core, utls): auto-merge armed for every update type — a routine bump is typically minor/patch, not major, so the file's major-only rule above doesn't reach these. Safety is entirely the required checks' job (Test ex-ray (Go), and check-vendoring-integrity riding inside Lint), not this rule.

Don't update the vendored trees' own go.mod/go.sum under crates/ex-ray/third_party/*/. They're pristine upstream code (see VENDORING.md), excluded from this repo's tooling, and pull-subrepo's own allowlist silently overwrites them with upstream's version on the next bump anyway.

github.com/v2fly/v2ray-core/v5 and github.com/refraction-networking/utls in crates/ex-ray/go.mod are locally `replace`d to the vendored third_party trees (see VENDORING.md) — .gitrepo's branch, not this require line, is authoritative for their version. check-vendoring-integrity treats a mismatch as a violation; only finish-vendor-bump may bump this line, in lockstep with .gitrepo.

Rust compiler: its own reviewable PR, never automerged. A compiler bump lands new default-on clippy lints across the whole workspace at once (#855), so it must not ride in a batch. `groupName: null` un-groups it; `automerge: false` overrides the major-updates rule above, which matches every manager including this one. Last rule wins — these compiler rules must stay LAST in this array.

Go compiler: `crates/ex-ray/go.mod`'s `toolchain` directive (what actions/setup-go installs) and its `go` directive (the language level) move in ONE PR. Split across two PRs they can transiently land as `go` > `toolchain`, which the Go tool rejects and `gomodTidy` then fails on. Never automerged, same reason as Rust.

The `go` directive is a range under `go-mod-directive` versioning, so the default `replace` strategy yields no update — `bump` is the documented opt-in. Scoped to depType `golang`; the `toolchain` directive is an exact semver and needs no strategy override.
